clue.text: Extra pissed bondage freak's exhortation?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: more drunk, the comparative of a slang word for drunk
second meaning: what someone being tied up might urge about the ropes

explanation.walkthrough: Pissed is British slang for drunk, not angry; the comparative of tight in that sense is the first meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is informal for drunk, so its comparative means more drunk; the cry to pull bonds firmer is the same word.

clue.text: (& 24dn.) Pissed off 'Tone' — an excellent end!

parts.note: high is slang for intoxicated

indicators.note: something gone off has spoiled and lost its proper form, so the quoted word is rearranged

parts.note: the quoted word, taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed by a musical tone nonetheless salutes a fine finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pissed off' reads as one phrase meaning annoyed, but it splits in two: pissed means intoxicated, and off is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To end on a high note is an idiom for finishing at a moment of success, so the phrase names a triumphant close.

clue.text: Tricky Nixon farts on quitting, getting stick

indicators.note: tricky suggests something devious and twisted, so the remaining letters are scrambled
quitting means leaving, so the little word on departs from the fodder

parts.note: the former US president, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tricky Dick Nixon breaks wind while leaving office and takes some flak for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Tricky Dick was Nixon's nickname, so 'Tricky Nixon' reads as one name. Removing ON from NIXON FARTS leaves NIXFARTS, which rearranges to TRANSFIX.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfix is to pierce through with a pointed weapon, which is one sense of to stick, as in sticking a pig.

clue.text: Reject half of Mr Bean with electronic insert

indicators.note: an insert is something put inside, so the electronic letter goes into the middle
with places the bean word alongside the kept letter
half of a two-letter title keeps just one of its letters, here the latter

parts.note: the second of the two letters of the title
E is the standard abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
a bean is an example of a pulse, an edible seed of a legume

explanation.surface: Someone rebuffs half of Rowan Atkinson's comic character with an electronic gadget fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr Bean' looks like the TV character, but it splits: Mr loses half, Bean is the vegetable. The E sits between R and PULSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To repulse an attack or an offer is to drive it back or turn it down, a straightforward synonym of reject.

clue.text: Country agent's fit of pique, getting end away after party

indicators.note: the end being sent away means the final letter of the sulking word is dropped
after puts the shortened word following the party word

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the British political party
a sulk is a bout of resentful moodiness

explanation.surface: A diplomat throws a tantrum and then has sex after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting one's end away' is British slang for having sex, which is the surface joke; here it just drops the K from SULK.
explanation.definitionFit: A consul is an official stationed abroad who represents a nation's interests and citizens, so an agent of a state.

clue.text: see 11ac.
Soldier is contrary during simulated relief — delicate work

indicators.note: being contrary means going the opposite way, so the soldier is read backwards
something happening during another event sits inside it, so the soldier goes within
simulated means faked, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A cussed soldier takes part in an exercise of mock relief operations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simulated relief' looks like a sculptural term for raised carving, apt to delicate work, but simulated is just the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Filigree is ornamental work of fine twisted wire, so it is a delicate piece of craftsmanship.

clue.text: Shit way to intervene in floundering euro

indicators.note: intervening means coming between, so the way word is placed inside the other letters
floundering means struggling clumsily, so the currency name is thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A crude complaint about a crap plan to bail out the struggling European currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordure is a formal word for excrement or dung, so it names the same stuff as the vulgar noun.

clue.text: Trouble taken by lady I'm screwing to provide a rag

indicators.note: the trouble word is taken on by the twisted letters, attaching to their end
screwing means twisting round, so the letters of the lady phrase are turned about

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
taken as written, apostrophe dropped
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A man boasts that the woman he is sleeping with brings trouble with her, all reported in a tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Mail is a British right-wing tabloid newspaper; rag is a contemptuous word for a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag is a disparaging term for a low-quality newspaper, and Private Eye routinely applies it to this tabloid.

clue.text: In which big party donors doubtless appear to relish nuts being busted on pocketing House?

definitions.text: In which big party donors doubtless appear

indicators.note: pocketing means putting into one's pocket, so the House abbreviation is held inside
busted means broken apart, so the preceding words are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A sneer at rich party donors who love having their nuts squeezed while pocketing a seat in the Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: The British honours list names people given knighthoods, peerages and the like, and is often accused of rewarding party donors.
explanation.definitionFit: The cryptic definition describes the published roll of awards and titles, where generous funders of a party are widely suspected of turning up.

clue.text: (& 6dn.) FBI messed with "OBE" t-shirts? Good luck to 'em!

indicators.note: messed with means tampered with and jumbled, so all these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the honour, taken as written
taken as written, hyphen dropped

explanation.surface: The FBI meddles with T-shirts printed with a British honour, and the setter wishes them luck.
explanation.walkthrough: An OBE is a British honour (Officer of the Order of the British Empire). 'Best of British' is short for 'the best of British luck', said wishing someone well, often ironically.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiomatic British way of wishing someone success, frequently with a sarcastic undertone, just like the exclamation.

clue.text: It selects fancy balls

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamented, so the letters are worked into a new pattern

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Something that chooses elegant dances or social occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy balls' reads as glamorous dances, but fancy is the anagram signal and balls is the vulgar definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Balls is common slang for the male reproductive glands, so it means the same body parts in coarse terms.

clue.text: Soft Obama's behind dope

parts.note: soft can mean foolish or feeble-minded
ass is the American word for the backside, hence a US president's

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about the softness of Barack Obama's bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: Obama signals an Americanism: the British word would be arse.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid person, and a silly ass is a mild, old-fashioned British insult for a fool.

clue.text: Provocative Ms Bercow's possibly lost everything for old flame

indicators.note: losing one thing in exchange for another is a swap, so a chunk of the name is replaced

parts.note: Sally Bercow, outspoken wife of the former Commons Speaker John Bercow; possibly marks her as one example of the name
all means everything
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Sally Bercow, perhaps, lost the lot in exchange for a former lover.
explanation.walkthrough: SALLY with ALL taken out and EX put in its place leaves S-EX-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexy means sexually alluring, and provocative can describe dress or behaviour designed to arouse desire.

clue.text: (& 22ac.) Steered all clear of pussy protector?

indicators.note: steered means driven or guided along a new course, so the letters are redirected into another order

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone took care to stay well away from a woman's private parts, with a nudge-nudge question mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Pussy is meant as a cat, not the vulgar sense the surface invites.
explanation.definitionFit: A collar treated with insecticide is worn by cats and dogs to ward off parasites, so it guards a pet cat.

clue.text: Jinxed Russell finally cut down on sex? F-off!

indicators.note: F-off tells you to take the letter F off the front of the sex word
in a down clue one piece written on another sits after it
finally points to the last letter of the name before it

parts.note: the last letter of the name
the vulgar word for sex
less means reduced or cut down in amount

explanation.surface: Comedian Russell Brand, ill-starred at last, is told to rein in his famous sex life and is sent packing.
explanation.walkthrough: Russell Brand is a British comedian known for his womanising; F-off is a coy form of the expletive, here meaning remove F.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone jinxed has bad fortune following them, and luckless means having no good fortune at all, an exact match.

clue.text: Ex-jailbird dumped on society, as heard on radio

definitions.note: a radio programme, defined by a description rather than a noun

indicators.note: in a down clue the ex-jailbird is dumped on top of the society letter

parts.note: Jeffrey Archer, novelist and Tory peer jailed for perjury in 2001
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A former convict gets tipped out onto society, as reported in a radio bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap opera about farming folk, broadcast daily.
explanation.definitionFit: The serial is a radio-only drama, so it is something listeners hear on the wireless rather than see.

clue.text: Dandy's upset over screw — female is the decider

indicators.note: the dandy word lies over and around the screw word, enclosing it
upset means turned upside down, which in a down clue reads the dandy word upwards

parts.note: a fop is a vain man overly concerned with dress
lay is slang for a sexual partner or act, as is screw
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A dandy is upset about some sex, and a woman settles the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, upset turns a word upside down, and over lets the reversed word straddle the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A play-off is an extra match held to settle a tie or a final ranking, so it is the deciding game.

clue.text: Anorak's past cracking cryptic clue

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so the past word goes inside the other letters
cryptic means puzzling and obscure, so the next word is disguised by rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A crossword nerd's history of solving difficult cryptic clues.
explanation.walkthrough: Anorak in British slang is a geek, which suits the crossword surface; here it is the waterproof jacket. A cagoule is a lightweight hooded waterproof.
explanation.definitionFit: An anorak is a hooded weatherproof jacket, and a cagoule is a light pull-over kind of the same garment.

clue.text: Olive, say, having strain of flu gets pregnant the old-fashioned way

indicators.note: having means possessing as well, so the second part is joined on after the first

parts.note: an olive is botanically an example of a fruit

indicators.note: a strain is a variant form, so the illness word appears in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Olive catches influenza and also falls pregnant by traditional means rather than IVF.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old-fashioned way' looks like a coy surface phrase about sex, but it flags the archaic sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In older usage, as in the Biblical 'be fruitful and multiply', the word meant fertile or bearing offspring, hence with child.

clue.text: Even accommodating a large body is flash

definitions.note: a verb here, to show off, which matches the verb answer even though the surface makes flash look like an adjective meaning showy

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so the level word holds the body inside

parts.note: flat means level or even
the UN, the United Nations, is a large international body

explanation.surface: A level surface with room for a big body is showy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A large body' sounds like a fat person, but it is an international organisation. 'Is flash' reads as showy, yet flash is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To flash something is to display it ostentatiously, and to flaunt it is to show it off in the same way.

clue.text: see 15ac.
Maybe Paris welcomes vaguely lyrical name for a high profile candidate

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

clue.text: see 2dn.
Cooler new home for Max Clifford

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for a jail
second meaning: where the celebrity publicist was sent after his 2014 conviction for indecent assault

explanation.walkthrough: Max Clifford was a British PR man jailed in 2014; Cooler looks like a comparative adjective but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The cooler is old slang for a jail, and the publicist was sentenced to eight years behind bars, so it became his residence.

clue.text: Tight on gas, producing verbal diarrhoea

indicators.note: one word on another means the two are set side by side, the first ahead

parts.note: fast means firmly fixed or tight, as in hold fast
gas is informal for idle chatter

explanation.surface: Someone short of fuel, or holding in wind, ends up talking a load of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Tight and gas suggest drink and wind; they are fixed-firm and chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast talk is rapid glib persuasive speech, and verbal diarrhoea is a jokey idiom for an unstoppable stream of words.
